 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal information-determining axis sets, so \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{proof}

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal information-determining axis sets, so \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{proof}

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal information-determining axis sets, so \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{proof}

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal information-determining axis sets, so \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{proof}

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal information-determining axis sets, so \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{proof}

+is unique, and non-unique-or-absent otherwise.
+\item[Indexed refinement system.]
+A family of state-refinement relations indexed by information coordinates,
+each monotone for the state preorder and the specified time order.
+\item[Information-determining axis set.]
+A finite set of refinement coordinates whose information values determine any
+decided truth value among the states reachable along those coordinates.
+\item[Pairwise commuting refinements and common refinement.]
+Refinements for which every indicated finite family has a state refining all
+its members.
+\item[Readout-preserving rewrite.]
+A rewrite between partial outputs that preserves both definedness and value.
+\item[Banded groupoid lift of a support presheaf.]
+A category fibred in groupoids whose presheaf of isomorphism classes is the
+given empirical-model support presheaf and whose automorphism sheaves are the
+specified band.
 \end{description}

\subsubsection{Componentwise obstruction monotonicity}

The obstruction theory of \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} becomes dynamic once global component sections and their component gerbes are transported along refinement. In the model classes just described, the basic structural fact is that refinement can only reveal more branch-level visible information; it cannot re-hide information that was already uniformly visible.

\begin{proposition}[Refinement monotonicity of branch visibility]\label{thm:branch-visibility-monotonicity}
Let $q\le p$, let $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ be admitted at both states, and write
\[
a_p=[r]_p,
\qquad
a_q=[r]_q.
\]
Assume:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item there is a morphism of slice sites
\[
f_{q,p}:\mathcal C_{q,s}/a_q\to \mathcal C_{p,s}/a_p;
\]
\item the banded groupoid lift at $q$ is equivalent to the pullback of the banded groupoid lift at $p$ along $f_{q,p}$;
\item global component sections pull back along refinement, and for a branch $w\in \Vis_{q,s}(r)$ lying above $v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)$ the corresponding component gerbes satisfy
\[
\mathfrak G_w\simeq f_{q,p}^*(\mathfrak G_v);
\]
\item compatible finite nerve representatives have been chosen together with a simplicial refinement map
\[
N(f_{q,p}):N(\mathcal U_q)\to N(\mathcal U_p)
\]
such that the induced component obstruction classes satisfy
\[
\omega_w=N(f_{q,p})^*(\omega_v)
\]
with the same finite abelian band $A$.
\end{enumerate}
Then
\[
X_v\subseteq X_w,
\qquad
K_w\subseteq K_v,
\qquad
A_{\mathrm{vis}}^w\twoheadrightarrow A_{\mathrm{vis}}^v,
\qquad
|K_w|\le |K_v|.
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The pullback of gerbes is again a gerbe, and the induced cohomology class is the pullback of the original one \cite[Tag 06NY]{StacksProject}, \cite[Theorem~3.11]{BerghSchnurer2021}. Naturality of the universal coefficient map with respect to the simplicial refinement map $N(f_{q,p})$ gives the cohomological compatibility needed below. Let $\chi\in X_v$. Then
\[
\chi_*(\omega_v)=0.
\]
Applying the pullback $N(f_{q,p})^*$ gives
\[
\chi_*(\omega_w)=\chi_*\bigl(N(f_{q,p})^*(\omega_v)\bigr)=N(f_{q,p})^*\bigl(\chi_*(\omega_v)\bigr)=0,
\]
so $\chi\in X_w$. Hence $X_v\subseteq X_w$.

By \Cref{thm:intrinsic-visible-quotient},
\[
K_v=\bigcap_{\chi\in X_v}\ker\chi
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
K_w=\bigcap_{\chi\in X_w}\ker\chi.
\]
Since $X_v\subseteq X_w$, intersecting over the larger family gives the smaller subgroup, so $K_w\subseteq K_v$. Therefore the quotient map $A\twoheadrightarrow A/K_v$ factors through $A/K_w$, yielding a surjection
\[
A_{\mathrm{vis}}^w=A/K_w\twoheadrightarrow A/K_v=A_{\mathrm{vis}}^v.
\]
For finite groups, $K_w\subseteq K_v$ implies $|K_w|\le |K_v|$.
\end{proof}

\begin{example}[A strict drop under refinement]\label{ex:refinement-drop}
Let $A=\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z$, and let $r$ be admitted at $q\le p$.
Assume that at $p$ there is one global component section $v$ and a component obstruction class
\[
\omega_v\in H^2(N(\mathcal U_p),A)
\]
with
\[
K_v=\langle 2\rangle\subseteq A.
\]
Hence
\[
A_{\mathrm{vis}}^v=A/K_v\cong \mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z.
\]

Suppose $r$ has a unique branch $w$ above $v$ at the refinement $q$, and the induced pullback class
\[
\omega_w=f_{q,p}^*(\omega_v)
\]
is trivial in $H^2(N(\mathcal U_q),A)$. Then
\[
K_w=\{0\},\qquad A_{\mathrm{vis}}^w=A/K_w\cong A.
\]
By \Cref{thm:branch-visibility-monotonicity}, the map
\[
A_{\mathrm{vis}}^w\longrightarrow A_{\mathrm{vis}}^v
\]
is the quotient mod~$2$, so $|K_w|<|K_v|$ and the strict hidden budget decreases under this refinement.
\end{example}

\begin{corollary}[Refinement decreases presentation-relative hidden branch budget]\label{cor:branch-budget-monotonicity}
Under the hypotheses of \Cref{thm:branch-visibility-monotonicity}, refinement can only enlarge the quotient and can never increase the presentation-relative minimum auxiliary register size of the branch:
\[
\log_2|K_w|\le \log_2|K_v|.
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
This is the last clause of \Cref{thm:branch-visibility-monotonicity} rewritten on a logarithmic scale.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{Readout-preserving rewrites}

\begin{definition}[Readout-preserving rewrite]\label{def:value-preserving-rewrite}
A \emph{readout expression} is any term whose semantic role at a state is determined by a typed readout. A rewrite
\[
E\leadsto E'
\]
between readout expressions is \emph{value preserving} if for every state $p$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item $\Read_p(E)$ is defined if and only if $\Read_p(E')$ is defined,
\item whenever defined, $\Read_p(E)=\Read_p(E')$.
\end{enumerate}

 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal information-determining axis sets, so \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{proof}

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal information-determining axis sets, so \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{proof}

\section{Aggregation over component sections}\label{sec:branch-aggregation}

We compare the quotients attached to the different global component sections of a single admissible parameter. Retaining the component label leads to a label-aware quotient, while forgetting it leads to a common-character quotient. The comparison results below are formal once the family of componentwise homological image subgroups have been fixed, whereas the construction theorems later in the section remain internal to explicitly chosen finite nerves and constant bands.

\begin{definition}[Family of componentwise homological image subgroups]\label{def:branchwise-intrinsic-data}
Fix an admissible parameter $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ at a state $p$, and assume:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item the hypotheses of \Cref{def:cech-gluing-obstruction} hold;
\item the set $\Vis_{p,s}(r)$ is finite and nonempty;
\item every component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ is banded by the same finite abelian group $A$ and admits a finite nerve representative of its component obstruction class $\omega_v$.
\end{enumerate}
For each global component section $v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)$, write
\[
K_v:=K_{\omega_v},
\qquad
Q_v:=Q_{\omega_v}=A/K_v,
\qquad
\pi_v:A\twoheadrightarrow Q_v.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Label-aware quotient]\label{thm:branch-sensitive-visible-quotient}
In the setting of \Cref{def:branchwise-intrinsic-data}, consider the diagonal map
\[
\Delta_{\mathrm{lab}}:A\longrightarrow \prod_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} Q_v,
\qquad
x\longmapsto (\pi_v(x))_v.
\]
Then
\[
\ker(\Delta_{\mathrm{lab}})=\bigcap_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v.
\]
Consequently, the quotient
\[
Q_{\mathrm{lab}}(r):=A\Big/\bigcap_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v
\]
is canonically isomorphic to $\mathrm{Im}(\Delta_{\mathrm{lab}})$. It is the maximal quotient of $A$ detected by the family of componentwise quotient maps when the component label is retained.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For $x\in A$ one has $\Delta_{\mathrm{lab}}(x)=0$ if and only if $\pi_v(x)=0$ for every global component section $v$, which is equivalent to $x\in K_v$ for every $v$. Hence
\[
\ker(\Delta_{\mathrm{lab}})=\bigcap_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v.
\]
The first isomorphism theorem therefore yields
\[
\mathrm{Im}(\Delta_{\mathrm{lab}})
\cong
A\Big/\bigcap_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v.
\]
Thus, once the global component section is known, two elements of $A$ have the same image exactly when they have the same image in every componentwise quotient.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Common-character quotient]\label{thm:branch-uniform-visible-quotient}
In the setting of \Cref{def:branchwise-intrinsic-data}, let
\[
X_v:=\{\chi\in \widehat A\mid \chi_*(\omega_v)=0\}
\]
for each global component section $v$, and define the common annihilating characters by
\[
X^{\mathrm{com}}(r):=\bigcap_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} X_v.
\]
Then
\[
X^{\mathrm{com}}(r)=\mathrm{Ann}\Bigl(\sum_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v\Bigr).
\]
Consequently, the quotient
\[
Q_{\mathrm{com}}(r):=A\Big/\sum_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v
\]
is exactly the quotient detected by the characters that annihilate every componentwise homological image simultaneously.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{thm:intrinsic-visible-quotient}, one has
\[
X_v=\mathrm{Ann}(K_v)
\]
for every $v$. Therefore
\[
X^{\mathrm{com}}(r)
=
\bigcap_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} \mathrm{Ann}(K_v)
=
\mathrm{Ann}\Bigl(\sum_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v\Bigr),
\]
where the last identity is the standard annihilator formula for finite abelian groups \cite[Part~I, Chap.~2]{Terras1999}. Finite abelian duality then gives
\[
\bigcap_{\chi\in X^{\mathrm{com}}(r)} \ker\chi
=
\sum_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v.
\]
Hence the quotient detected by all common annihilating characters is precisely
\[
A\Big/\sum_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v.
\qedhere
\]
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Canonical comparison and component-forgetting kernel]\label{def:branch-comparison-map}
In the setting of \Cref{def:branchwise-intrinsic-data}, let
\[
\pi_{\mathrm{lab}}:A\twoheadrightarrow Q_{\mathrm{lab}}(r)
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\pi_{\mathrm{com}}:A\twoheadrightarrow Q_{\mathrm{com}}(r)
\]
be the canonical quotient maps. Since
\[
\bigcap_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v
\subseteq
\sum_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v,
\]
there is a unique surjective homomorphism
\[
\beta_r:Q_{\mathrm{lab}}(r)\twoheadrightarrow Q_{\mathrm{com}}(r)
\]
such that
\[
\beta_r\circ \pi_{\mathrm{lab}}=\pi_{\mathrm{com}}.
\]
Its kernel is denoted
\[
K_{\mathrm{forg}}(r):=
\ker(\beta_r)
\cong
\Bigl(\sum_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v\Bigr)\Big/\Bigl(\bigcap_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v\Bigr)
\]
and called the \emph{component-forgetting kernel}.
\end{definition}

 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]

+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.

 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. +For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. +For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause.  \end{proof}

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal information-determining axis sets, so \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{proof}

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal information-determining axis sets, so \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{proof}

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal information-determining axis sets, so \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{proof}

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal information-determining axis sets, so \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{proof}

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial.  \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal information-determining axis sets, so \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{proof}

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal information-determining axis sets, so \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{proof}

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal information-determining axis sets, so \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Dual character description of the component-forgetting kernel]\label{cor:branch-resolution-dual}
In the setting of \Cref{def:branch-comparison-map},
\[
\widehat{Q_{\mathrm{lab}}(r)}
\cong
\sum_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} X_v,
\qquad
\widehat{Q_{\mathrm{com}}(r)}
\cong
\bigcap_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} X_v.
\]
Moreover,
\[
\widehat{K_{\mathrm{forg}}(r)}
\cong
\Bigl(\sum_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} X_v\Bigr)\Big/\Bigl(\bigcap_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} X_v\Bigr).
\]
Thus the dual of the component-forgetting kernel consists of the characters generated by the componentwise class-trivializing characters, modulo those that are common to every component.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{thm:intrinsic-visible-quotient}, one has
\[
X_v=\mathrm{Ann}(K_v)
\]
for every global component section $v$. Finite abelian duality then gives
\[
\widehat{Q_{\mathrm{lab}}(r)}
\cong
\mathrm{Ann}\Bigl(\bigcap_v K_v\Bigr)
=
\sum_v \mathrm{Ann}(K_v)
=
\sum_v X_v
\]
and, by \Cref{thm:branch-uniform-visible-quotient},
\[
\widehat{Q_{\mathrm{com}}(r)}
\cong
\bigcap_v X_v.
\]
Dualizing the short exact sequence of \Cref{thm:branch-comparison-exact-sequence} yields an exact sequence
\[
0\longrightarrow \widehat{Q_{\mathrm{com}}(r)}
\longrightarrow \widehat{Q_{\mathrm{lab}}(r)}
\longrightarrow \widehat{K_{\mathrm{forg}}(r)}
\longrightarrow 0,
\]
and substituting the two identifications above gives the claimed quotient description of $\widehat{K_{\mathrm{forg}}(r)}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Auxiliary register for the component-forgetting map]\label{def:branch-resolution-code}
In the setting of \Cref{def:branch-comparison-map}, a \emph{auxiliary register for the component-forgetting map} consists of a finite set $R$ and an injective map
\[
\iota_{\mathrm{forg}}:Q_{\mathrm{lab}}(r)\hookrightarrow Q_{\mathrm{com}}(r)\times R
\]
such that
\[
\mathrm{pr}_1\circ \iota_{\mathrm{forg}}=\beta_r.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact logarithmic component-forgetting fibre cardinality]\label{thm:branch-resolution-budget}
Every auxiliary register for the component-forgetting map satisfies
\[
|R|\ge |K_{\mathrm{forg}}(r)|
=
\left|\Bigl(\sum_v K_v\Bigr)\Big/\Bigl(\bigcap_v K_v\Bigr)\right|.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\log_2|R|
\ge
\log_2|K_{\mathrm{forg}}(r)|.
\]
This bound is sharp.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Since $\mathrm{pr}_1\circ \iota_{\mathrm{forg}}=\beta_r$, every fiber of $\beta_r$ injects into $R$. By \Cref{thm:branch-comparison-exact-sequence}, each fiber of $\beta_r$ is a coset of $K_{\mathrm{forg}}(r)$ and therefore has cardinality $|K_{\mathrm{forg}}(r)|$. Hence
\[
|R|\ge |K_{\mathrm{forg}}(r)|.
\]

For sharpness, choose a finite set $R$ with
\[
|R|=|K_{\mathrm{forg}}(r)|.
\]
Choose a set-theoretic section
\[
s:Q_{\mathrm{com}}(r)\to Q_{\mathrm{lab}}(r)
\]
of $\beta_r$, and choose an injection
\[
j:K_{\mathrm{forg}}(r)\hookrightarrow R.
\]
Define
\[
\iota_{\mathrm{forg}}(x):=
\bigl(\beta_r(x),j(x-s(\beta_r(x)))\bigr).
\]
Since $x-s(\beta_r(x))\in \ker(\beta_r)=K_{\mathrm{forg}}(r)$, the map is well defined. If
\[
\iota_{\mathrm{forg}}(x)=\iota_{\mathrm{forg}}(y),
\]
then $\beta_r(x)=\beta_r(y)$ and
\[
j(x-s(\beta_r(x)))=j(y-s(\beta_r(y))).
\]
Injectivity of $j$ gives $x=y$, so $\iota_{\mathrm{forg}}$ is injective and the bound is attained.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Factorization of uniform quotient-fibre information]\label{cor:uniform-hidden-budget-factorization}
In the setting of \Cref{def:branch-comparison-map},
\[
\left|\sum_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v\right|
=
|K_{\mathrm{forg}}(r)|
\cdot
\left|\bigcap_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v\right|.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\log_2\left|\sum_v K_v\right|
=
\log_2|K_{\mathrm{forg}}(r)|
+
\log_2\left|\bigcap_v K_v\right|.
\]
Thus the logarithmic fibre cardinality of the common-character quotient splits into the component-forgetting contribution and the logarithmic cardinality of the intersection of the componentwise images.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{def:branch-comparison-map},
\[
|K_{\mathrm{forg}}(r)|
=
\left|\Bigl(\sum_v K_v\Bigr)\Big/\Bigl(\bigcap_v K_v\Bigr)\right|
=
\frac{|\sum_v K_v|}{|\bigcap_v K_v|}.
\]
Rearranging gives the first displayed identity, and the second follows after taking base-$2$ logarithms.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Common auxiliary register for the componentwise quotient maps]\label{def:branch-preserving-strictification-code}
In the setting of \Cref{def:branchwise-intrinsic-data}, a \emph{common auxiliary register for the componentwise quotient maps} consists of a finite set $R$ and, for each global component section $v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)$, an injective map
\[
\iota_v:A\hookrightarrow Q_v\times R
\]
such that
\[
\mathrm{pr}_1\circ \iota_v=\pi_v.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Common-register fibre cardinality]\label{thm:multi-branch-strictification-budget}
Every common auxiliary register for the componentwise quotient maps satisfies
\[
|R|\ge \max_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} |K_v|.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\log_2|R|\ge \max_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} \log_2|K_v|.
\]
This bound is sharp.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Fix a global component section $v$. Since $\mathrm{pr}_1\circ \iota_v=\pi_v$, every fiber of $\pi_v$ injects into $R$. By \Cref{def:intrinsic-visible-quotient}, every fiber of $\pi_v$ is a coset of $K_v$ and hence has cardinality $|K_v|$. Therefore $|R|\ge |K_v|$ for every $v$, which proves the lower bound.

For sharpness, choose a finite set $R$ with
\[
|R|=\max_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} |K_v|.
\]
For each $v$, choose an injection
\[
j_v:K_v\hookrightarrow R
\]
and a set-theoretic section
\[
s_v:Q_v\to A
\]
of $\pi_v$. Define
\[
\iota_v(x):=\bigl(\pi_v(x),j_v(x-s_v(\pi_v(x)))\bigr).
\]
Since $x-s_v(\pi_v(x))\in K_v$, the formula is well defined. If $\iota_v(x)=\iota_v(y)$, then $\pi_v(x)=\pi_v(y)$ and
\[
j_v(x-s_v(\pi_v(x)))=j_v(y-s_v(\pi_v(y))).
\]
Injectivity of $j_v$ gives $x=y$. Thus each $\iota_v$ is injective, so the bound is attained.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Single-component reduction]\label{cor:single-branch-reduction}
If
\[
\Vis_{p,s}(r)=\{v\},
\]
then
\[
Q_{\mathrm{lab}}(r)\cong Q_{\mathrm{com}}(r)\cong Q_v
\]
and the minimum common auxiliary-register cardinality is exactly $|K_v|$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
If there is only one global component section, then
\[
\bigcap_{u\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_u
=
\sum_{u\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_u
=
K_v.
\]
The quotient statements follow from \Cref{thm:branch-sensitive-visible-quotient,thm:branch-uniform-visible-quotient}, and the register-size statement is \Cref{thm:multi-branch-strictification-budget}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Nonzero UCT-Ext classes and vanishing $H_2$ evaluation]\label{thm:character-blind-obstructions}
In the setting of \Cref{def:finite-nerve-presentation}, with a chosen admissible
parameter, global component section, banded groupoid lift, trivialized constant finite
abelian band $A$, and the \textup{(H4)} comparison datum needed to regard
$\omega$ as a derived component class, the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item $K_{\omega}=0$;
\item $Q_{\omega}=A$;
\item $\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}=0$;
\item $\omega$ lies in the subgroup
\[
\operatorname{Ext}^1(H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),A)\subseteq H^2(N(\mathcal U),A).
\]
\end{enumerate}
If these conditions hold and $\omega\neq 0$, then the chosen component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ is non-neutral, while every character of $A$ is class-trivializing for that component class. If, in addition, the banded groupoid lift is essentially surjective on the terminal fibre, \(F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}\) is separated on the slice, and $|\Vis_{p,s}(r)|=1$, then
\[
M,p\Vdash \NoAmalg_s(r).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{def:intrinsic-visible-quotient},
\[
K_{\omega}=\mathrm{Im}(\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}),
\]
so \textup{(i)} and \textup{(iii)} are equivalent. Since $Q_{\omega}=A/K_{\omega}$, conditions \textup{(i)} and \textup{(ii)} are equivalent. By the universal coefficient sequence, \textup{(iii)} holds exactly when $\omega\in\ker(\eta_A)$, and this kernel is the stated $\operatorname{Ext}$-subgroup. Hence all four conditions are equivalent.

If they hold and $\omega\neq 0$, then \Cref{prop:derived-branch-classification} shows that the component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ is non-neutral.
On the other hand, $\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}=0$ implies
\[
\chi\circ \mathrm{ev}_{\omega}=0
\]
for every $\chi\in\widehat A$, so \Cref{thm:intrinsic-visible-quotient} shows that every character is class-trivializing.

Assume now that \(F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}\) is separated on the slice and that $|\Vis_{p,s}(r)|=1$. Since the chosen global component section $v$ exists, \Cref{prop:compsecs-vs-visible-branches} gives
\[
M,p\Vdash \CompSec_s(r).
\]
Suppose towards a contradiction that
\[
M,p\Vdash \Sec_s(r).
\]
By \Cref{def:realization-prestack}(i), this yields an object of the terminal fibre $(\mathfrak P_r)_a$, and its image under the stackification morphism
\[
\iota_r:\mathfrak P_r\to \mathfrak L_r
\]
defines an object of $\mathfrak L_r(a)$. Because there is only one global component section, every object of $\mathfrak L_r(a)$ lies in the unique component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v(a)$. Hence
\[
\mathfrak G_v(a)\neq\varnothing.
\]
By \Cref{lem:terminal-fibre-neutrality}, this implies that $\mathfrak G_v$ is neutral, contradicting the non-neutrality already proved. Therefore
\[
M,p\nVdash \Sec_s(r).
\]
Combining this with $M,p\Vdash \CompSec_s(r)$ and admissibility of $r$, we obtain
\[
M,p\Vdash \NoAmalg_s(r).
\]
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Vanishing evaluation when $H_2=0$]\label{cor:h2-vanishing-blindness}
Assume
\[
H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)=0.
\]
Then, for every obstruction class $\omega\in H^2(N(\mathcal U),A)$,
\[
\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}=0,
\qquad
K_{\omega}=0,
\qquad
Q_{\omega}=A.
\]
Every nonzero component obstruction class on such a nerve therefore has zero $H_2$ evaluation, and every character is class-trivializing.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
If $H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)=0$, then
\[
\mathrm{Hom}(H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),A)=0,
\]
so $\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}=0$ for every $\omega$. Apply \Cref{thm:character-blind-obstructions}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[No nonzero classes with vanishing $H_2$ evaluation when $H_1$ is free]\label{cor:h1-free-no-blindness}
Assume that $H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)$ is free abelian. Then
\[
K_{\omega}=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\omega=0.
\]
Equivalently, every nonzero component obstruction class has nonzero $H_2$ evaluation. In particular, if $|\Vis_{p,s}(r)|=1$, every nonzero component obstruction class on such a nerve produces a proper homological cokernel.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
If $H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)$ is free abelian, then
\[
\operatorname{Ext}^1(H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),A)=0.
\]
Hence the universal coefficient map $\eta_A$ is injective. By \Cref{thm:character-blind-obstructions},
\[
K_{\omega}=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\eta_A(\omega)=0.
\]
Injectivity of $\eta_A$ therefore gives $K_{\omega}=0$ if and only if $\omega=0$. If $\omega\neq 0$, then $K_{\omega}\neq 0$, so $Q_{\omega}=A/K_{\omega}$ is a proper quotient of the finite group $A$.
\end{proof}

\begin{example}[A nonzero class with vanishing $H_2$ evaluation on an $\mathbb{R}P^2$-type nerve]\label{ex:rp2-character-blind}
This is a finite-nerve mechanism example.  Let $\mathcal U$ be a finite cover
whose \v{C}ech nerve is a finite triangulation of $\mathbb{R}P^2$, and take
\[
A=\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z.
\]
Then
\[
H_2(\mathbb{R}P^2,\mathbb Z)=0,
\qquad
H_1(\mathbb{R}P^2,\mathbb Z)\cong \mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z
\]
\cite[Sec.~2.2]{Hatcher2002}. The universal coefficient sequence therefore yields
\[
H^2(\mathbb{R}P^2,\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z)
\cong
\operatorname{Ext}^1(\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z,\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z)
\cong
\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z
\]
\cite[Sec.~3.1]{Hatcher2002}. Let $\omega$ be the nonzero class. Then
\[
\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}=0,
\qquad
K_{\omega}=0,
\qquad
Q_{\omega}=A,
\]
by \Cref{thm:character-blind-obstructions}. Thus the homological cokernel is all of $A$, although the obstruction class is nonzero. Every character is therefore class-trivializing. If this is the unique global component section of the admissible parameter under consideration and \(F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}\) is separated on the slice, then \Cref{thm:gerbe-null-semantics} yields a matching family without global amalgamation whose component class is trivialized by every character.

The last sentence is conditional on the usual banded-stack-lift data: an
admissible parameter, a banded stack lift with constant band
$\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$, essential surjectivity on the terminal fibre, and the
\textup{(H4)} comparison identifying the displayed finite-nerve class with the
derived component class; the matching-without-amalgamation conclusion also requires
separatedness on the slice site associated to the parameter.  The unconditional content of the example is the
homological mechanism
\[
\omega\in \operatorname{Ext}^1(H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),A),
\qquad
\eta_A(\omega)=0,
\]
which makes the homological cokernel equal to $A$ although the
obstruction class is nonzero.  Thus the example records the UCT
$\operatorname{Ext}^1$ kernel of the finite nerve, while the component-gerbe conclusion
enters only after the admissible-parameter and banded-lift hypotheses have been
supplied.
\end{example}

\begin{example}[A single-component surjective-homological-evaluation class on $S^2$]\label{ex:s2-single-branch-maximal-collapse}
Let $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to S^2\}_{i\in I}$ be a finite good cover of $S^2$, let $N:=N(\mathcal U)$ be its nerve, and let $\mathcal C_a$ be the corresponding slice site for one admissible parameter $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ with $a=[r]_p$. Take the constant band
\[
A=\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z
\]
on $\mathcal C_a$. Define the presheaf of local sections
\[
F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}:\mathcal C_a^{op}\to\mathsf{Set}
\]
by
\[

\]

\subsection{Homological images, cokernels, and annihilating characters}

\begin{definition}[Homological image and cokernel]\label{def:intrinsic-visible-quotient}
In the setting of \Cref{def:finite-nerve-presentation}, define the \emph{presentation-relative homological image subgroup}
\[
K_{\omega}:=\mathrm{Im}(\mathrm{ev}_{\omega})
\]
and the associated \emph{homological cokernel}
\[
Q_{\omega}:=\operatorname{coker}(\mathrm{ev}_{\omega})=A/K_{\omega}.
\]
These terms are relative to the presentation-comparison groupoid of
\Cref{def:finite-nerve-comparison-relation}; no presentation-free quotient is
asserted outside that groupoid.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Class-trivializing characters]\label{def:class-admissible-character}
In the setting of \Cref{def:finite-nerve-presentation}, let
\[
X_{\omega}:=\{\chi\in\widehat A\mid \chi_*(\omega)=0\},
\qquad
\widehat A:=\mathrm{Hom}(A,\mathbb T).
\]
Elements of $X_{\omega}$ are called \emph{class-trivializing} for $\omega$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Character-theoretic detection of the homological cokernel]\label{thm:intrinsic-visible-quotient}
In the setting of \Cref{def:class-admissible-character},
\[
X_{\omega}
=
\{\chi\in\widehat A\mid \chi\circ \mathrm{ev}_{\omega}=0\}
=
\mathrm{Ann}(K_{\omega}).
\]
Consequently,
\[
K_{\omega}
=
\bigcap_{\chi\in X_{\omega}}\ker\chi,
\qquad
Q_{\omega}\cong A\Big/\!\bigcap_{\chi\in X_{\omega}}\ker\chi.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For every character $\chi:A\to\mathbb T$, naturality of the universal coefficient sequence gives a commutative square
\[
\begin{CD}
H^2(N(\mathcal U),A) @>\eta_A>> \mathrm{Hom}(H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),A) \\
@V\chi_*VV @VV(\chi\circ -)V \\
H^2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb T) @>\eta_{\mathbb T}>> \mathrm{Hom}(H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),\mathbb T).
\end{CD}
\]
Since $\mathbb T$ is divisible and hence injective in $\mathbf{Ab}$, one has
\[
\operatorname{Ext}^1(H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),\mathbb T)=0
\]
\cite[Sec.~2.3]{Weibel1994}. Thus $\eta_{\mathbb T}$ is an isomorphism by \Cref{def:finite-nerve-presentation}. Therefore
\[
\chi_*(\omega)=0
\Longleftrightarrow
\eta_{\mathbb T}(\chi_*(\omega))=0
\Longleftrightarrow
\chi\circ \eta_A(\omega)=0
\Longleftrightarrow
\chi\circ \mathrm{ev}_{\omega}=0.
\]
This proves the first displayed identity, and the second is simply the definition of the annihilator of a subgroup of $A$.

Let $H:=K_{\omega}=\mathrm{Im}(\mathrm{ev}_{\omega})\le A$. By the first part of the proof, $X_{\omega}=\mathrm{Ann}(H)$. Finite abelian duality implies
\[
\bigcap_{\chi\in \mathrm{Ann}(H)}\ker\chi=H
\]
\cite[Part~I, Chaps.~2, 12]{Terras1999}. Hence
\[
K_{\omega}
=
\bigcap_{\chi\in X_{\omega}}\ker\chi.
\]
The final isomorphism follows immediately:
\[
Q_{\omega}
=
A/K_{\omega}
\cong
A\Big/\!\bigcap_{\chi\in X_{\omega}}\ker\chi.
\qedhere
\]
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Character detection of the homological cokernel]\label{cor:intrinsic-character-detection}
The quotient map
\[
\pi_{\omega}:A\twoheadrightarrow Q_{\omega}
\]
induces a natural isomorphism
\[
\widehat{Q_{\omega}}\cong X_{\omega}.
\]
For elements $x,y\in A$, one has
\[
\pi_{\omega}(x)=\pi_{\omega}(y)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\chi(x)=\chi(y)\ \text{for every class-trivializing }\chi.
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{thm:intrinsic-visible-quotient},
\[
X_{\omega}=\mathrm{Ann}(K_{\omega})=K_{\omega}^{\perp}.
\]
Characters of $Q_{\omega}=A/K_{\omega}$ are exactly the characters of $A$ that kill $K_{\omega}$, so precomposition with $\pi_{\omega}$ identifies $\widehat{Q_{\omega}}$ with $X_{\omega}$. The separation statement follows from finite abelian duality applied to the finite group $Q_{\omega}$ \cite[Part~I, Chap.~2]{Terras1999}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Initiality among zero-evaluation quotients]\label{thm:intrinsic-pure-ext-initiality}
In the finite nerve representative of \Cref{def:finite-nerve-presentation}, let
\[
\pi_\omega:A\twoheadrightarrow Q_\omega=A/K_\omega
\]
be the homological cokernel. For every surjective homomorphism $q:A\twoheadrightarrow B$, the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item $q$ factors uniquely through $\pi_\omega$;
\item $q$ kills $\operatorname{Im}(\mathrm{ev}_\omega)=K_\omega$;
\item $\eta_B(q_*\omega)=0$;
\item $q_*(\omega)$ lies in the UCT $\operatorname{Ext}^1$ subgroup
\[
\operatorname{Ext}^1(H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),B)
\subseteq H^2(N(\mathcal U),B)
\]
of the universal coefficient sequence.
\end{enumerate}
Thus $Q_\omega$ is initial among coefficient quotients for which the pushed-forward obstruction has zero $H_2$ evaluation. This is the pullback-site, finite-nerve form of the companion initiality theorem \cite[Theorem~6.13]{MaZhang2026ConditionalGluingFailure}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The equivalence of \textup{(i)} and \textup{(ii)} is the universal property of the quotient
\[
\pi_\omega:A\twoheadrightarrow A/K_\omega.
\]
Indeed, a homomorphism $q:A\to B$ factors uniquely through $\pi_\omega$ if and only if $K_\omega\subseteq\ker q$, which is exactly the assertion that $q$ kills $\operatorname{Im}(\mathrm{ev}_\omega)$.

For \textup{(ii)} and \textup{(iii)}, use naturality of the universal coefficient map with respect to the coefficient homomorphism $q$. The naturality square gives
\[
\eta_B(q_*\omega)=q\circ \eta_A(\omega)=q\circ \mathrm{ev}_\omega.
\]
Thus $\eta_B(q_*\omega)=0$ if and only if $q$ vanishes on the image of $\mathrm{ev}_\omega$, namely on $K_\omega$.

Finally, the universal coefficient exact sequence for the finite nerve is
\[
0\to \operatorname{Ext}^1(H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),B)
\to H^2(N(\mathcal U),B)
\xrightarrow{\eta_B}
\operatorname{Hom}(H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),B)
\to 0.
\]
Therefore $\eta_B(q_*\omega)=0$ if and only if $q_*(\omega)$ lies in the kernel of $\eta_B$, which is precisely the displayed UCT $\operatorname{Ext}^1$ subgroup. This proves all equivalences and the initiality statement.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Class-trivializing initiality when $H_1$ vanishes]\label{cor:h1-vanishing-class-trivializing}
Assume
\[
H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)=0.
\]
Then, for every surjective homomorphism $q:A\twoheadrightarrow B$, the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item $q_*(\omega)=0$ in $H^2(N(\mathcal U),B)$;
\item $q$ factors uniquely through
\[
\pi_{\omega}:A\twoheadrightarrow Q_{\omega}.
\]
\end{enumerate}
Hence, when $H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)=0$, the homological cokernel is initial among coefficient quotients that annihilate the obstruction class itself.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
If $H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)=0$, then
\[
\operatorname{Ext}^1(H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),B)=0
\]
for every abelian group $B$. Thus, in the criterion of \Cref{thm:intrinsic-pure-ext-initiality}, the zero-evaluation condition is equivalent to $q_*(\omega)=0$, and the conclusion follows.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Presentation-relative invariance without a canonical splitting]\label{rem:no-canonical-splitting}
For a fixed finite nerve representative, the quotient
$Q_{\omega}$ and the subgroup
$K_{\omega}=\mathrm{Im}(\mathrm{ev}_{\omega})$ are invariants of the chosen
presentation. Across comparison-equivalent presentations they are transported
functorially only along chosen morphisms in the presentation-comparison
groupoid, as in \Cref{prop:invariance-visible-quotients}; different zigzags
with the same endpoints may carry different coefficient automorphisms. By
contrast, the universal coefficient sequence need not split canonically. Thus
the theory isolates a homological cokernel and homological image subgroup
at each presentation, with comparison-zigzag functoriality, without requiring
any noncanonical decomposition of $\omega$ into $H_2$-evaluated and UCT-Ext
summands.
\end{remark}

\begin{corollary}[Comparison with cocycle-coordinate quotients]\label{cor:strict-to-intrinsic-visible}
Let $\alpha$ be any finite \v{C}ech cocycle representative of the class $\omega$. Then the homological cokernel
\[
Q_{\omega}
\]
admits a canonical surjective homomorphism onto the cocycle-coordinate quotient
\[
A/H_\alpha.
\]
Equivalently, every cocycle-coordinate quotient is a quotient of the homological cokernel.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Let $q:A\twoheadrightarrow A/H_\alpha$ be the canonical quotient. By \Cref{thm:initial-visible-quotient}, the quotient kills every cocycle value $\alpha_{ijk}$ pointwise, so the pushed-forward cocycle representative is zero. Hence $q_*(\omega)=0$, and in particular it lies in the $\operatorname{Ext}$-subgroup of $H^2(N(\mathcal U),A/H_\alpha)$. Apply \Cref{thm:intrinsic-pure-ext-initiality}.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Chain-level evaluation of a presentation]\label{def:chain-level-evaluation}

\widetilde\alpha:C_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)\to A
\]
defined by linear extension from the oriented $2$-simplices:
\[
\widetilde\alpha\!\left(\sum_{\sigma} n_{\sigma}\sigma\right)
:=
\sum_{\sigma} n_{\sigma}\alpha(\sigma).
