\begin{definition}[Auxiliary register for the homological quotient]\label{def:intrinsic-strictification-code}
An \emph{auxiliary register for the homological quotient} for the obstruction class $\omega$ consists of a finite set $R$ and an injective map
\[
\iota_{\omega}:A\hookrightarrow Q_{\omega}\times R
\]
such that
\[
\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\iota_{\omega}=\pi_{\omega}.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Fibre size of the homological quotient]\label{cor:intrinsic-hidden-state-lower-bound}
Every auxiliary register for the homological quotient satisfies
\[
|R|\ge |K_{\omega}|.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\log_2|R|\ge \log_2|K_{\omega}|.
\]
This lower bound is sharp.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{def:intrinsic-visible-quotient}, the fibres of $\pi_{\omega}$ are exactly the cosets of $K_{\omega}$, so every fibre has cardinality $|K_{\omega}|$. The same fibre-counting argument as in \Cref{thm:minimal-information-cost-of-strictification} therefore shows that any auxiliary register preserving the first projection must satisfy $|R|\ge |K_{\omega}|$.

For sharpness, take $R:=K_{\omega}$ and choose a set-theoretic section $s_{\omega}:Q_{\omega}\to A$ of $\pi_{\omega}$. Then
\[
\iota_{\omega}(x):=\bigl(\pi_{\omega}(x),x-s_{\omega}(\pi_{\omega}(x))\bigr)
\]
is injective.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Prime decomposition of the homological quotient and fibre size]\label{thm:intrinsic-prime-decomposition}
Write the finite abelian group $A$ as a direct sum of its $p$-primary components:
\[
A=\bigoplus_p A_{(p)}.
\]
Let $\omega_p\in H^2(N(\mathcal U),A_{(p)})$ be the image of $\omega$ under the projection onto the $p$-primary summand. Then
\[
\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}=\bigoplus_p \mathrm{ev}_{\omega_p},
\qquad
K_{\omega}=\bigoplus_p K_{\omega,p},
\qquad
Q_{\omega}\cong \bigoplus_p A_{(p)}/K_{\omega,p},
\]
where
\[
K_{\omega,p}:=\mathrm{Im}(\mathrm{ev}_{\omega_p}).
\]
Consequently,
\[
|K_{\omega}|=\prod_p |K_{\omega,p}|,
\qquad
\log_2|K_{\omega}|=\sum_p \log_2|K_{\omega,p}|.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Both $H^2(N(\mathcal U),-)$ and $\mathrm{Hom}(H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),-)$ commute with finite direct sums, so the universal coefficient map is compatible with the primary decomposition of $A$. Hence
\[
\eta_A(\omega)=\bigoplus_p \eta_{A_{(p)}}(\omega_p),
\]
which is exactly the asserted decomposition of $\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}$.

Taking images gives
\[
K_{\omega}
=
\mathrm{Im}(\mathrm{ev}_{\omega})
=
\bigoplus_p \mathrm{Im}(\mathrm{ev}_{\omega_p})
=
\bigoplus_p K_{\omega,p},
\]
by \Cref{def:intrinsic-visible-quotient}. The quotient decomposition follows immediately:
\[
Q_{\omega}
=
A/K_{\omega}
\cong
\bigoplus_p A_{(p)}/K_{\omega,p}.
\]
Since finite direct sums correspond to products of cardinalities, the logarithmic fibre-cardinality formula is immediate.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Homological versus chain-coordinate fibre size]\label{cor:strict-intrinsic-budget-comparison}
For every finite \v{C}ech cocycle representative $\alpha$ of the class $\omega$,
\[
|K_{\omega}|\le |H_\alpha|,
\qquad
\log_2|K_{\omega}|\le \log_2|H_\alpha|.
\]
Hence the minimum auxiliary register size for the homological quotient never exceeds that for the cocycle-coordinate quotient. Equality holds if and only if the canonical surjection
\[
Q_{\omega}\twoheadrightarrow A/H_\alpha
\]
is an isomorphism.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{cor:strict-to-intrinsic-visible}, there is a surjective homomorphism
\[
Q_{\omega}=A/K_{\omega}\twoheadrightarrow A/H_\alpha.
\]
For finite groups this implies
\[
|A|/|K_{\omega}|\ge |A|/|H_\alpha|,
\]
hence $|K_{\omega}|\le |H_\alpha|$. The logarithmic inequality is immediate. Equality of cardinalities holds exactly when the displayed surjection is bijective.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Surjective homological evaluation]\label{cor:maximal-collapse}
In the setting of \Cref{def:finite-nerve-presentation}, the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item $\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}:H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)\to A$ is surjective;
\item $K_{\omega}=A$;
\item $Q_{\omega}=0$;
\item the logarithmic fibre cardinality of the homological quotient is $\log_2|A|$:
\[
\log_2|K_{\omega}|=\log_2|A|.
\]
\end{enumerate}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{def:intrinsic-visible-quotient}, $K_{\omega}=\mathrm{Im}(\mathrm{ev}_{\omega})$, so \textup{(i)} and \textup{(ii)} are equivalent. Condition \textup{(ii)} is equivalent to \textup{(iii)} by the definition of $Q_{\omega}=A/K_{\omega}$. For finite groups, \textup{(ii)} is also equivalent to $|K_{\omega}|=|A|$, which is exactly \textup{(iv)} after taking $\log_2$.
\end{proof}

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal information-determining axis sets, so \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{proof}

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal information-determining axis sets, so \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{proof}

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal information-determining axis sets, so \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{proof}

\subsection{Quotients and choice of compatible representatives}

We now fix one global component section and a finite \v{C}ech cocycle representative. The cocycle-coordinate quotient $A/H_\alpha$ kills the subgroup generated by the coordinates of this chosen cocycle; the homological cokernel considered in the next section removes dependence on the cocycle representative within the specified presentation-comparison groupoid.

\begin{definition}[Ordered \v{C}ech convention]\label{def:ordered-cech-convention}
For every finite cover
\[
\mathcal U=\{a_i\to a\}_{i\in I}
\]
used in a finite \v{C}ech cocycle representative, fix a total order on $I$. The
group $\check C^n(\mathcal U,A)$ is indexed by strictly increasing
nondegenerate tuples
\[
i_0<\cdots<i_n
\]
whose overlap $a_{i_0\cdots i_n}$ is nonempty. If a value is written on an
arbitrary ordered tuple, it denotes the alternating extension from the
increasing tuple: permuting pairwise distinct indices multiplies the value
by the sign of the permutation, and a tuple with a repeated index has value
$0$. In degree $2$, the cocycle identity on every ordered nondegenerate
quadruple is
\[
\alpha_{jkl}-\alpha_{ikl}+\alpha_{ijl}-\alpha_{ijk}=0.
\]
Thus reversing the orientation of a nondegenerate triple replaces
$\alpha_{ijk}$ by $-\alpha_{ijk}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Finite \v{C}ech cocycle representative]\label{def:finite-obstruction-presentation}
Fix an admissible parameter $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ at a state $p$, and assume:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item the hypotheses of \Cref{def:cech-gluing-obstruction} hold;
\item a global component section
\[
v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)
\]
has been chosen;
\item the associated component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ is banded by a finite abelian group $A$,
\item a finite covering family
\[
\mathcal U=\{a_i\to a\}_{i\in I},
\qquad
a=[r]_p,
\]
has been chosen together with a \v{C}ech $2$-cocycle
\[
\alpha=(\alpha_{ijk})\in Z^2(\mathcal U,A)
\]
representing the component obstruction class $\omega_v$, written in the ordered
convention of \Cref{def:ordered-cech-convention}.
\end{enumerate}
Define the \emph{coordinate-image subgroup}
\[
H_\alpha:=\langle \alpha_{ijk}\mid i<j<k\text{ and }a_{ijk}\neq\varnothing\rangle\le A,
\]
and the associated \emph{cocycle-coordinate quotient}
\[
Q_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{coord}}:=A/H_\alpha.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{remark}[Orientation independence of the generated subgroup]\label{rem:strict-subgroup-orientation}
The definition of $H_\alpha$ is independent of whether one generates from
increasing triples or from all oriented nondegenerate triples. Indeed, any
orientation change replaces a generator $\alpha_{ijk}$ by
$-\alpha_{ijk}$, and the subgroup generated by a subset of an abelian group
is unchanged after replacing any generator by its negative. Degenerate
triples contribute $0$ by \Cref{def:ordered-cech-convention}.
\end{remark}

\begin{theorem}[Cocycle-coordinate quotient]\label{thm:initial-visible-quotient}
In the setting of \Cref{def:finite-obstruction-presentation}, let
\[
\pi:A\twoheadrightarrow Q_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{coord}}
\]
be the canonical quotient map. Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item the pushed-forward cocycle $\pi_*(\alpha)$ is pointwise zero on every nonempty triple overlap;
\item if $\varphi:A\to B$ is any homomorphism into an abelian group $B$ such that $\varphi(\alpha_{ijk})=0$ for every ordered nondegenerate triple overlap, then there exists a unique homomorphism
\[
\bar\varphi:Q_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{coord}}\to B
\]
with $\varphi=\bar\varphi\circ\pi$.
\end{enumerate}
Hence \(Q_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{coord}}\) is the elementary quotient of \(A\) by the
subgroup generated by the displayed cocycle values; equivalently, it is the
initial coefficient quotient through which this chosen obstruction
cocycle representative becomes pointwise zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By construction and \Cref{rem:strict-subgroup-orientation}, every oriented
cocycle value $\alpha_{ijk}$ lies in the subgroup $H_\alpha$. Therefore
$\pi(\alpha_{ijk})=0$ for every ordered nondegenerate triple overlap, which
proves (i).

For (ii), the hypothesis $\varphi(\alpha_{ijk})=0$ on every ordered
nondegenerate triple overlap implies that every generator of $H_\alpha$
lies in $\ker\varphi$. Hence $H_\alpha\subseteq\ker\varphi$. By the
universal property of the quotient by $H_\alpha$, there exists a unique
homomorphism $\bar\varphi:A/H_\alpha\to B$ satisfying
$\varphi=\bar\varphi\circ\pi$.
\end{proof}

The cocycle-coordinate quotient $A/H_\alpha$ depends on the chosen cocycle representative $\alpha$, not only on the cohomology class $\omega_v$. The next section removes this dependence: the homological evaluation map $\mathrm{ev}_\omega$ is defined from the class itself, and its cokernel $Q_\omega$ is invariant within the homology-equivalent comparison class isolated there. The comparison between the two quotients is given by \Cref{cor:strict-to-intrinsic-visible} and \Cref{prop:chain-vs-homological-visibility}.

\begin{definition}[Coboundary action and annihilating characters]\label{def:gauge-invariance-character}
In the setting of \Cref{def:finite-obstruction-presentation}, the \v{C}ech $1$-cochain group $C^1(\mathcal U,A)$ acts on cocycles by coboundary translation: a cochain
\[
h=(h_{ij})\in C^1(\mathcal U,A)
\]
sends a cocycle $\alpha$ to the cohomologous cocycle
\[
(h\cdot\alpha)_{ijk}:=\alpha_{ijk}+(\delta h)_{ijk}.
\]
A character $\chi\in\widehat A$ is said to \emph{annihilate the coordinate-image subgroup} if it kills $H_\alpha$, equivalently if it factors through the quotient
\[
\pi:A\twoheadrightarrow Q_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{coord}}=A/H_\alpha.
\]
In that case the pushed-forward class $\chi_*[\alpha]$ depends only on the quotient and not on the chosen local trivializations.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Characters of the cocycle-coordinate quotient]\label{thm:character-definability-barrier}
In the setting of \Cref{def:finite-obstruction-presentation}, let
\[
\widehat A:=\mathrm{Hom}(A,\mathbb T),
\]
where $\mathbb T\subseteq\mathbb C^\times$ is the unit circle, and define
\[
H_\alpha^\perp:=\{\chi\in\widehat A\mid \chi(h)=1\text{ for every }h\in H_\alpha\}.
\]
Call a character $\chi\in\widehat A$ \emph{cocycle-trivializing} for the chosen representative if
\[
\chi(\alpha_{ijk})=1
\]
for every nonempty triple overlap of $\mathcal U$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item a character $\chi\in\widehat A$ is cocycle-trivializing if and only if $\chi\in H_\alpha^\perp$;
\item the quotient map $\pi:A\twoheadrightarrow Q_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{coord}}$ induces a natural isomorphism
\[
\widehat{Q_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{coord}}}\cong H_\alpha^\perp;
\]
\item consequently, every cocycle-trivializing character factors uniquely through $Q_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{coord}}$, and a character annihilates the coordinate-image subgroup if and only if it lies in $H_\alpha^\perp$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Since $H_\alpha$ is generated by the cocycle values $\alpha_{ijk}$, a character $\chi$ is trivial on $H_\alpha$ if and only if it is trivial on each generator $\alpha_{ijk}$. This proves (i).

For (ii), the quotient map $\pi$ induces by precomposition an injective homomorphism
\[
\pi^*:\widehat{Q_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{coord}}}\hookrightarrow \widehat A.
\]
Its image consists exactly of the characters on $A$ that are trivial on $\ker\pi=H_\alpha$, namely $H_\alpha^\perp$. Thus $\pi^*$ identifies $\widehat{Q_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{coord}}}$ with $H_\alpha^\perp$.

Clause \textup{(iii)} is just \Cref{def:gauge-invariance-character} rewritten using \textup{(i)} and \textup{(ii)}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Detection by annihilating characters]\label{cor:visible-quotient-character-separation}
In the setting of \Cref{def:finite-obstruction-presentation}, for elements $x,y\in A$ the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item $\pi(x)=\pi(y)$ in $Q_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{coord}}$;
\item $\chi(x)=\chi(y)$ for every cocycle-trivializing character $\chi\in\widehat A$.
\end{enumerate}
Equivalently, $Q_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{coord}}$ is the quotient of $A$ obtained by identifying exactly those elements that cannot be separated by cocycle-trivializing characters.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Assume first that $\pi(x)=\pi(y)$. By \Cref{thm:character-definability-barrier}(ii), every cocycle-trivializing character $\chi$ factors as
\[
\chi=\bar\chi\circ\pi
\]
for a unique character $\bar\chi\in\widehat{Q_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{coord}}}$. Hence
\[
\chi(x)=\bar\chi(\pi(x))=\bar\chi(\pi(y))=\chi(y).
\]

Conversely, suppose $\pi(x)\neq\pi(y)$. Then
\[
g:=\pi(x)-\pi(y)\neq 0
\]
in the finite abelian group $Q_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{coord}}$. By the structure theorem for finite abelian groups \cite{DummitFoote2004}, there is an isomorphism
\[
Q_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{coord}}\cong \mathbb Z/n_1\mathbb Z\oplus\cdots\oplus \mathbb Z/n_t\mathbb Z
\]
under which the image of $g$ has some nonzero coordinate, say the $k$th. The coordinate character
\[
\psi(z_1,\dots,z_t):=\exp(2\pi i z_k/n_k)
\]
therefore satisfies $\psi(g)\neq 1$. By \Cref{thm:character-definability-barrier}(ii), the character
\[
\chi:=\psi\circ\pi
\]
is globally admissible. Since
\[
\chi(x)\chi(y)^{-1}=\psi(\pi(x)-\pi(y))=\psi(g)\neq 1,
\]
we have $\chi(x)\neq\chi(y)$, contradicting (ii). Thus $\pi(x)=\pi(y)$.
\end{proof}
\leanverified{paper_gluing_failure_visible_quotient_character_separation}

\begin{definition}[Fibre-separating auxiliary register]\label{def:auxiliary-strictification-code}
In the setting of \Cref{def:finite-obstruction-presentation}, an \emph{fibre-separating auxiliary register} consists of a finite set $R$ and an injective map
\[
\iota:A\hookrightarrow Q_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{coord}}\times R
\]
such that the first projection recovers the canonical quotient:
\[
\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\iota=\pi.
\]
Equivalently, the quotient is kept fixed, while the auxiliary register $R$ separates elements inside each fibre of $\pi$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Fibre size of an auxiliary register]\label{thm:minimal-information-cost-of-strictification}
In the setting of \Cref{def:auxiliary-strictification-code}, every fibre-separating auxiliary register satisfies
\[
|R|\ge |H_\alpha|.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\log_2 |R|\ge \log_2 |H_\alpha|.
\]
Moreover, this lower bound is sharp.
\leanverified{paper_gluing_failure_minimal_information_cost_of_choice of compatible representatives}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Let $\bar a\in Q_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{coord}}$. The fiber $\pi^{-1}(\bar a)$ is a coset of $\ker\pi=H_\alpha$, hence has cardinality $|H_\alpha|$. Since $\iota$ is injective and $\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\iota=\pi$, the restriction of $\iota$ to $\pi^{-1}(\bar a)$ lands inside the slice $\{\bar a\}\times R$ and remains injective. Therefore
\[
|H_\alpha|=|\pi^{-1}(\bar a)|\le |\{\bar a\}\times R|=|R|.
\]
This proves the lower bound.

To see that it is sharp, take $R:=H_\alpha$. Choose a set-theoretic section $s:Q_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{coord}}\to A$ of $\pi$. For each $x\in A$, the difference
\[
h(x):=x-s(\pi(x))
\]
lies in $H_\alpha$. Define
\[
\iota(x):=(\pi(x),h(x))\in Q_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{coord}}\times H_\alpha.
\]
Then $\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\iota=\pi$. If $\iota(x)=\iota(y)$, then $\pi(x)=\pi(y)$ and $h(x)=h(y)$, hence
\[
x=s(\pi(x))+h(x)=s(\pi(y))+h(y)=y.
\]
Thus $\iota$ is injective and $|R|=|H_\alpha|$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Minimum auxiliary register size]\label{cor:conservative-recovery-budget}
For a finite \v{C}ech cocycle representative, an injective lift that leaves the quotient coordinate unchanged requires at least \(\log_2|H_\alpha|\) bits in its auxiliary register. This is the elementary fibre-counting consequence of quotienting by the coordinate-image subgroup \(H_\alpha\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Any such lift induces a fibre-separating auxiliary register in the sense of \Cref{def:auxiliary-strictification-code}. Apply \Cref{thm:minimal-information-cost-of-strictification}.
\end{proof}
\leanverified{paper_conservative_extension_conservative_recovery_budget}

\subsection{A worked finite example}

\begin{example}[A coordinate-image subgroup of order two]\label{ex:one-bit-hidden-obstruction}
Assume an admissible parameter $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ together with a three-member cover
\[
\mathcal U=\{a_0,a_1,a_2\to a\},
\qquad
a=[r]_p,
\]
and let the band be the additive group
\[
A=\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z.
\]
Suppose the chosen obstruction presentation is represented by a cocycle whose only nonzero value on a nonempty triple overlap is
\[
\alpha_{012}=2\in \mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z.
\]
Then
\[
H_\alpha=\langle 2\rangle=\{0,2\},
\qquad
Q_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{coord}}=A/H_\alpha\cong \mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z.
\]

Thus the quotient identifies $0$ with $2$ and identifies $1$ with $3$. By \Cref{thm:initial-visible-quotient}, this is the initial coefficient quotient through which the chosen cocycle representative becomes pointwise zero.

For $m\in\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z$, define a character
\[
\chi_m(x):=\exp(2\pi i mx/4).
\]
Then
\[
\chi_m(\alpha_{012})=\chi_m(2)=(-1)^m,
\]
so \Cref{thm:character-definability-barrier} implies that the cocycle-trivializing characters are exactly
\[
\chi_0
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\chi_2.
\]
Hence the only surviving linear detection is parity: $\chi_2$ distinguishes the two cosets of $H_\alpha$, while the phase-sensitive characters $\chi_1$ and $\chi_3$ do not factor through the quotient. By \Cref{cor:visible-quotient-character-separation}, the quotient is therefore exactly the quotient detected by all cocycle-trivializing characters.

Finally, \Cref{thm:minimal-information-cost-of-strictification} yields
\[
|R|\ge |H_\alpha|=2,
\]
so at least one auxiliary bit is required to distinguish all elements of $\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z$ while keeping the quotient coordinate fixed. This lower bound is attained by the auxiliary register
\[
0\mapsto (\overline{0},0),\qquad
2\mapsto (\overline{0},1),\qquad
1\mapsto (\overline{1},0),\qquad
3\mapsto (\overline{1},1),
\]
where $\overline{0},\overline{1}\in Q_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{coord}}\cong \mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$ and the second component is a one-bit register.
\end{example}

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal information-determining axis sets, so \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{proof}

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal information-determining axis sets, so \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{proof}

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal information-determining axis sets, so \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{proof}

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal information-determining axis sets, so \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Banded stack lift of the component sheaf]\label{def:realization-stack-extension}
For an admissible parameter $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ at a state $p$, abbreviate
\[
a=[r]_p,
\qquad
\mathcal C_a:=\mathcal C_{p,s}/a,
\]
and fix an abelian sheaf $\Band$ on $\mathcal C_a$. Let $\mathfrak E_r$ be a
$\Band$-banded stack in groupoids on $\mathcal C_a$. A
\emph{$\Band$-banded stack lift of the component sheaf} is a pair
\[
(\mathfrak E_r,\epsilon_r)
\]
consisting of such a stack together with an isomorphism of sheaves
\[
\epsilon_r:\pi_0(\mathfrak E_r)\xrightarrow{\sim} a_{p,s}F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}
\]
on $\mathcal C_a$.

For a sheafified global section
\[
v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)\cong \bigl(a_{p,s}F_{p,s}\bigr)(a),
\]
the \emph{$v$-component substack} of $\mathfrak E_r$ is the full substack
\[
\mathfrak E_r[v](U):=
\bigl\{x\in \mathfrak E_r(U)\mid \epsilon_{r,U}([x])=v|_U\bigr\}
\]
for objects $U$ of $\mathcal C_a$, where $\epsilon_{r,U}$ denotes the component of $\epsilon_r$ at $U$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Equivalence data and component transport]\label{lem:extension-equivalence-component-transport}
Let
\[
(\mathfrak E_r,\Band,\epsilon_r),
\qquad
(\mathfrak E'_r,\Band',\epsilon'_r)
\]
be banded stack lifts of the component sheaf on $\mathcal C_a$. Suppose an equivalence of stacks
\[
\Phi:\mathfrak E_r\to\mathfrak E'_r
\]
comes with a band isomorphism $\theta:\Band\xrightarrow{\sim}\Band'$ and satisfies
\[
\epsilon'_r\circ\pi_0(\Phi)=\epsilon_r.
\]
Then, for every sheafified global section $v$, $\Phi$ restricts to an equivalence of full component substacks
\[
\Phi_v:\mathfrak E_r[v]\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathfrak E'_r[v],
\]
and this restricted equivalence is banded by $\theta$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Let $U$ be an object of $\mathcal C_a$ and let $x\in\mathfrak E_r[v](U)$. By definition,
\[
\epsilon_{r,U}([x])=v|_U.
\]
The compatibility condition gives
\[
\epsilon'_{r,U}([\Phi(x)])
=
(\epsilon'_r\circ\pi_0(\Phi))_U([x])
=
\epsilon_{r,U}([x])
=
v|_U.
\]
Thus $\Phi(x)\in\mathfrak E'_r[v](U)$, so $\Phi$ restricts to a functor
\[
\Phi_v:\mathfrak E_r[v]\to\mathfrak E'_r[v].
\]
Since both component substacks are full, $\Phi_v$ is fully faithful because $\Phi$ is. For local essential surjectivity, take $z\in\mathfrak E'_r[v](U)$. A quasi-inverse $\Psi$ to $\Phi$ gives, after possibly refining $U$, an object $y\in\mathfrak E_r(U)$ with $\Phi(y)\cong z$. Applying $\epsilon'_r$ to this local isomorphism gives
\[
\epsilon_{r,U}([y])
=
\epsilon'_{r,U}([\Phi(y)])
=
\epsilon'_{r,U}([z])
=
v|_U,
\]
so $y$ lies locally in $\mathfrak E_r[v]$. Hence $\Phi_v$ is an equivalence of stacks. The automorphism-sheaf maps of $\Phi_v$ are the restrictions of the automorphism-sheaf maps of $\Phi$, so the band is transported by the same isomorphism $\theta$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Transport of Giraud classes under banded equivalence]\label{lem:giraud-class-transport}
Let $\mathfrak G$ be a $\Band$-banded gerbe and let $\mathfrak G'$ be a $\Band'$-banded gerbe on the same site $\mathcal C$. Suppose
\[
\Phi:\mathfrak G\to\mathfrak G'
\]
is an equivalence of stacks whose induced maps on automorphism sheaves identify the bands through an isomorphism
\[
\theta:\Band\xrightarrow{\sim}\Band'.
\]
Then
\[
\theta_*[\mathfrak G]=[\mathfrak G']
\qquad\text{in}\qquad
H^2(\mathcal C,\Band').
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Choose a cover $\{U_i\to U\}$ which locally trivializes $\mathfrak G$, objects $x_i\in\mathfrak G(U_i)$, and descent isomorphisms
\[
\varphi_{ij}:x_i|_{U_{ij}}\xrightarrow{\sim}x_j|_{U_{ij}}.
\]
The usual Giraud cocycle $c_{ijk}\in\Band(U_{ijk})$ is defined by
\[
\varphi_{ik}^{-1}\varphi_{jk}\varphi_{ij}=c_{ijk}\in\operatorname{Aut}(x_i|_{U_{ijk}})\cong\Band(U_{ijk}).
\]
Applying $\Phi$ gives local lift objects $\Phi(x_i)$ of $\mathfrak G'$ and comparison isomorphisms $\Phi(\varphi_{ij})$. The corresponding defect is
\[
\Phi(\varphi_{ik})^{-1}\Phi(\varphi_{jk})\Phi(\varphi_{ij})
=
\Phi(c_{ijk}),
\]
which is identified with $\theta(c_{ijk})$ under the band isomorphism. Thus the transported local trivialization of $\mathfrak G'$ has cocycle $\theta_*(c)$. Refining the cover or changing the local lift objects changes both cocycles by the corresponding coboundary, exactly as in the standard local-trivialization classification of banded gerbes \cite[Chap.~IV]{Giraud1971}, \cite[Tag 06NY]{StacksProject}. Hence the cohomology class of $\mathfrak G'$ is $\theta_*[\mathfrak G]$.

The functoriality invoked here is the usual naturality of Giraud's classification with respect to a morphism of bands. Equivalently, the assignment
\[
(\mathfrak G,\Band)\longmapsto [\mathfrak G]\in H^2(\mathcal C,\Band)
\]
is functorial for banded equivalences: an equivalence of gerbes whose automorphism sheaves are identified by $\theta$ transports a local-object defect cocycle to its pointwise image under $\theta$, and this construction is independent of all choices after passage to cohomology.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical component-section obstruction map under banded stack lifts]\label{thm:intrinsic-branch-obstruction-extension}
Let $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ be admissible at a state $p$, write
\[
a=[r]_p,
\qquad
\mathcal C_a:=\mathcal C_{p,s}/a,
\]
and let
\[
(\mathfrak E_r,\Band,\epsilon_r)
\]
be a $\Band$-banded stack lift of the component sheaf in the sense of \Cref{def:realization-stack-extension}. Then the assignment
\[
\delta_{\mathfrak E_r}:\Vis_{p,s}(r)\longrightarrow H^2(\mathcal C_a,\Band),
\qquad
v\longmapsto [\mathfrak E_r[v]]
\]
is canonically defined, where $[\mathfrak E_r[v]]$ denotes the Giraud class of the $v$-component substack. More precisely:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item for every sheafified global section $v$, the full substack $\mathfrak E_r[v]$ is a $\Band$-banded gerbe on $\mathcal C_a$;
\item for every sheafified global section $v$,
\[
\delta_{\mathfrak E_r}(v)=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\mathfrak E_r[v]\ \text{is neutral}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\mathfrak E_r[v](a)\neq\varnothing;
\]
\item if
\[
(\mathfrak E'_r,\Band',\epsilon'_r)
\]
is another banded stack lift of the component sheaf and
\[
\Phi:\mathfrak E_r\to \mathfrak E'_r
\]
is an equivalence of stacks whose induced map on automorphism sheaves identifies the bands through an isomorphism
\[
\theta:\Band\xrightarrow{\sim}\Band'
\]
and whose map on connected components satisfies
\[
\epsilon'_r\circ \pi_0(\Phi)=\epsilon_r,
\]
then for every sheafified global section $v$ the functor $\Phi$ restricts to an equivalence
\[
\mathfrak E_r[v]\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathfrak E'_r[v]
\]
and
\[
\theta_*\bigl(\delta_{\mathfrak E_r}(v)\bigr)=\delta_{\mathfrak E'_r}(v)
\quad\text{in}\quad
H^2(\mathcal C_a,\Band');
\]
\item if $r$ admits a gluing-sensitive banded lift datum and
\[
\mathfrak E_r=\mathfrak L_r=a(\mathfrak P_r)
\]
is its stackification, then
\[
\delta_{\mathfrak E_r}(v)=\omega_v
\]
for every global component section $v$ for which \textup{(H4)} holds.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Fix a sheafified global section
\[
v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)\cong \bigl(a_{p,s}F_{p,s}\bigr)(a).
\]
Since $\mathfrak E_r$ is a stack in groupoids and $\mathfrak E_r[v]$ is a full substack, $\mathfrak E_r[v]$ is again a stack in groupoids.

Let $U$ be an object of $\mathcal C_a$. The section
\[
v|_U\in \bigl(a_{p,s}F_{p,s}\bigr)(U)\cong \pi_0(\mathfrak E_r)(U)
\]
is, by definition of the sheaf of connected components, locally represented by objects of $\mathfrak E_r$. Hence there exists a cover
\[
\{U_i\to U\}
\]
and objects
\[
x_i\in \mathfrak E_r(U_i)
\]
with
\[
\epsilon_{r,U_i}([x_i])=v|_{U_i}.
\]
Therefore
\[
(\mathfrak E_r[v])(U_i)\neq\varnothing
\]
for every $i$, so $\mathfrak E_r[v]$ is locally nonempty.

Now let
\[
x,y\in \mathfrak E_r[v](U).
\]
Then
\[
\epsilon_{r,U}([x])=\epsilon_{r,U}([y])=v|_U.
\]
Because $\epsilon_{r,U}$ is an isomorphism, the connected-component classes $[x]$ and $[y]$ in $\pi_0(\mathfrak E_r)(U)$ coincide. By the definition of $\pi_0(\mathfrak E_r)$, there exists a cover
\[
\{U_i\to U\}
\]
such that
\[
x|_{U_i}\cong y|_{U_i}
\qquad
(\forall i).
\]
Thus any two objects of $\mathfrak E_r[v](U)$ are locally isomorphic. The full substack $\mathfrak E_r[v]$ is therefore a gerbe \cite[Chap.~IV]{Giraud1971}, \cite[Tag 06NY]{StacksProject}. Since it is full inside the $\Band$-banded stack $\mathfrak E_r$, the automorphism sheaf of every object in $\mathfrak E_r[v]$ is still identified with $\Band$.

The preceding sentence is the band-preservation lemma used in this
argument: if \(P\) is \(\Band\)-banded and \(L=a(P)\), every object of \(L\)
is locally in the essential image of \(P\), and the automorphism sheaf of
that local representative is \(\Band\). Because automorphism presheaves are
sheafified in the stackification and the band identifications are compatible
with restriction, these local identifications descend and glue on overlaps.
Consequently every object of \(L\), and every object of a full component
substack, has automorphism sheaf locally identified with \(\Band\) in a way
compatible with descent. This proves \textup{(i)}.

Clause \textup{(i)} identifies $\mathfrak E_r[v]$ as a $\Band$-banded gerbe, so its Giraud class
\[
[\mathfrak E_r[v]]\in H^2(\mathcal C_a,\Band)
\]
is defined canonically \cite[Chap.~IV]{Giraud1971}, \cite[Tag 06NY]{StacksProject}. By the classification of banded gerbes, this class vanishes if and only if the gerbe is neutral. Since $a$ is the terminal object of the slice site $\mathcal C_a$, neutrality is equivalent to the existence of an object over $a$, namely
\[
\mathfrak E_r[v](a)\neq\varnothing.
\]
This proves \textup{(ii)}.

Assume now that $\Phi$ is an equivalence as in \textup{(iii)}. The compatibility condition
\[
\epsilon'_r\circ\pi_0(\Phi)=\epsilon_r
\]
first fixes the component on which the equivalence is allowed to act: an object whose component is $v|_U$ is sent to an object whose component is again $v|_U$. Hence \Cref{lem:extension-equivalence-component-transport} gives a restricted equivalence
\[
\Phi_v:\mathfrak E_r[v]\to \mathfrak E'_r[v]
\]
of the two $v$-component gerbes. This equivalence is not merely an abstract equivalence of stacks: on every local object $x$ the induced map
\[
\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathfrak E_r[v]}(x)\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathfrak E'_r[v]}(\Phi_v x)
\]
is the band map $\theta:\Band\to\Band'$. Therefore the local-trivialization cocycle defining the Giraud class of $\mathfrak E_r[v]$ is transported termwise by $\theta$ to the cocycle defining the class of $\mathfrak E'_r[v]$. By the band-functorial classification recalled in \Cref{lem:giraud-class-transport},
\[
\theta_*\bigl([\mathfrak E_r[v]]\bigr)=[\mathfrak E'_r[v]]
\]
in $H^2(\mathcal C_a,\Band')$. This is exactly the displayed identity in \textup{(iii)}.

For \textup{(iv)}, let $\mathfrak E_r=\mathfrak L_r=a(\mathfrak P_r)$. By \Cref{prop:stackification-components}, the stackification carries a canonical identification
\[
\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)\cong a_{p,s}F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a},
\]
so $\mathfrak L_r$ is a banded stack lift of the component sheaf. The $v$-component substack defined above is then exactly the component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ of \Cref{def:compatible-realization-stack}. On every cover
\[
\mathcal U\in \Cov_v^{\mathrm{acyc}}(a),
\]
\Cref{thm:cech-bridge-compatible-realizations} constructs the \v{C}ech class of this gerbe. The filtered colimit of those \v{C}ech classes is, by the standard classification of banded gerbes, the Giraud class of $\mathfrak G_v$, and hypothesis \textup{(H4)} identifies that colimit with the derived cohomology group
\[
H^2(\mathcal C_a,\Band).
\]
By \Cref{def:cech-gluing-obstruction}, the image of that same filtered system is precisely $\omega_v$. Therefore
\[
\delta_{\mathfrak E_r}(v)=[\mathfrak G_v]=\omega_v.
\]
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Supporting component gerbes of global component sections]\label{thm:component-gerbe-decomposition}
In the pullback-based setting of \Cref{def:compatible-realization-stack}, and using only the banded groupoid lift and component data fixed there, every global component section $v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)$ determines a full substack $\mathfrak G_v\subseteq \mathfrak L_r$ that is a banded $\Band$-gerbe over $\mathcal C_{p,s}/a$. In particular, neither essential surjectivity on the terminal fibre over $a$ nor the derived comparison hypothesis \textup{(H4)} is used here.
\end{theorem}

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. +For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. +For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause.  \end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Typed readout]\label{def:typed-readout}
Let $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ and a state $p$ be given. Define the \emph{typed readout} of $r$ at $p$ by
\[
\Read_{p,s}(r):=
\begin{cases}
\Inadm, & M,p\nVdash \Adm_s(r),\\[0.5ex]
v, & \Vis_{p,s}(r)=\{v\}\ \text{for some sheafified global section }v,\\[0.5ex]
\Indet, & M,p\Vdash \Adm_s(r)\ \text{and}\ \Vis_{p,s}(r)\neq\{v\}\ \text{for every }v.
\end{cases}
\]
Thus a determined readout occurs exactly when the admissible parameter carries a unique sheafified global section; $\Inadm$ denotes an inadmissible parameter and $\Indet$ denotes the non-unique-or-absent case.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Address before value]\label{prop:address-before-value}
If
\[
\Read_{p,s}(r)=v
\qquad\text{with}\qquad
v\notin\{\Inadm,\Indet\},
\]
then
\[
M,p\Vdash \Adm_s(r)
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
M,p\Vdash \CompSec_s(r).
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{def:typed-readout}, a readout outside $\{\Inadm,\Indet\}$ occurs only in the singleton case
\[
\Vis_{p,s}(r)=\{v\}.
\]
Sheafified global sections are defined only for admissible parameters, so $M,p\Vdash \Adm_s(r)$. The section $v$ has a matching-family representative, hence $M,p\Vdash \CompSec_s(r)$ by \Cref{def:visible-value-classes}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Criterion for a determined readout]\label{cor:nonnull-readout-criterion}
\[
\Read_{p,s}(r)=v
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\Vis_{p,s}(r)=\{v\}.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\Read_{p,s}(r)=\Indet
\]
if and only if $r$ is admissible and either $\Vis_{p,s}(r)=\varnothing$ or $|\Vis_{p,s}(r)|>1$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
This is immediate from \Cref{def:typed-readout}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Refinement stability of defined readouts]\label{prop:typed-readout-persistence}
Let $q\le p$, and suppose
\[
\Read_{p,s}(r)=v
\qquad\text{with}\qquad
v\notin\{\Inadm,\Indet\}.
\]
Then
\[
\Read_{q,s}(r)=v.
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Since $v\notin\{\Inadm,\Indet\}$, the readout at $p$ is represented by a unique sheafified global section. By the refinement-conservation hypothesis~\ref{hyp:refinement-conservation}, matching families restrict functorially from $q$ to $p$, and a uniquely determined section at $p$ cannot split under further refinement. Hence the same section $v$ remains unique at $q$, so \Cref{def:typed-readout} gives $\Read_{q,s}(r)=v$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Failures of global existence}

\begin{definition}[Inadmissibility and existence of global sections]\label{def:undef-total-null}
For an element $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ at a state $p$, define
\begin{align*}
M,p\Vdash \Inadm_s(r)
&\quad:\Longleftrightarrow\quad
M,p\nVdash \Adm_s(r),\\
M,p\Vdash \HasGlob_s(r)
&\quad:\Longleftrightarrow\quad
M,p\Vdash \Adm_s(r)\land \Sec_s(r),\\
M,p\Vdash \NoGlob_s(r)
&\quad:\Longleftrightarrow\quad
M,p\Vdash \Adm_s(r)\land \neg\Sec_s(r).
\end{align*}
Thus admissible parameters are partitioned according to whether a global section exists, while $\Inadm_s$ records inadmissibility.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Three failures of global existence]\label{def:null-failure-modes}
For an admissible parameter $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ at a state $p$, define
\begin{align*}
\NoLoc_s(r)
&\quad:\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\Adm_s(r)\land \neg\LocSec_s(r),\\
\NoMatch_s(r)
&\quad:\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\Adm_s(r)\land \LocSec_s(r)\land \neg\CompSec_s(r),\\
\NoAmalg_s(r)
&\quad:\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\Adm_s(r)\land \CompSec_s(r)\land \neg\Sec_s(r).
\end{align*}
They record, respectively, no local sections, local sections but no matching family, and a matching family without a global amalgamation.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[The three cases imply failure of global existence]\label{prop:null-modes-imply-null}
For every admissible parameter $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ at a state $p$,
\[
M,p\Vdash \NoLoc_s(r)\ \lor\ \NoMatch_s(r)\ \lor\ \NoAmalg_s(r)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
M,p\Vdash \NoGlob_s(r).
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
If $M,p\Vdash \NoLoc_s(r)$, then $r$ is admissible and $\LocSec_s(r)$ fails. By \Cref{prop:global-implies-compatible-local}, existence of a global section would imply local nonemptiness, so $\Sec_s(r)$ fails and hence $M,p\Vdash \NoGlob_s(r)$.

If $M,p\Vdash \NoMatch_s(r)$, then $r$ is admissible, local sections exist, but no matching family does. Again \Cref{prop:global-implies-compatible-local} shows that $\Sec_s(r)$ would imply $\CompSec_s(r)$, so $\Sec_s(r)$ fails and $M,p\Vdash \NoGlob_s(r)$.

If $M,p\Vdash \NoAmalg_s(r)$, then $r$ is admissible and $\Sec_s(r)$ fails by definition, so $M,p\Vdash \NoGlob_s(r)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Mutual exclusivity of the three cases]\label{prop:null-modes-exclusive}
No two distinct failure cases can hold simultaneously for the same parameter at the same state.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The case $\NoLoc_s(r)$ contains $\neg\LocSec_s(r)$, while the other two contain $\LocSec_s(r)$. The case $\NoMatch_s(r)$ contains $\neg\CompSec_s(r)$, while $\NoAmalg_s(r)$ contains $\CompSec_s(r)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Decidability of the local-section predicates]\label{def:decomposition-decidability}
Let $p$ be a state and $s\in S_{\mathrm{ref}}$. The local-section predicates are \emph{decided at $p$ for the sort $s$} if, for every admissible parameter
\[
r:\mathsf{Ref}_s
\]
at $p$, both predicates
\[
\LocSec_s(r)
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\CompSec_s(r)
\]
are decided at $p$ in the sense of \Cref{def:decidedness}.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Trichotomy for failure of global existence]\label{prop:null-trichotomy}
Assume that the local-section predicates are decided at $p$ for the sort $s$, and let
\[
r:\mathsf{Ref}_s
\]
be admissible at $p$. If
\[
M,p\Vdash \NoGlob_s(r),
\]
then exactly one of the three formulas
\[
\NoLoc_s(r),\qquad
\NoMatch_s(r),\qquad
\NoAmalg_s(r)
\]
holds at $p$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Since
\[
M,p\Vdash \NoGlob_s(r),
\]
the parameter $r$ is admissible and
\[
M,p\nVdash \Sec_s(r).
\]
Because the local-section predicates are decided at $p$ for the sort $s$, the formula $\LocSec_s(r)$ is decided.

If
\[
M,p\nVdash \LocSec_s(r),
\]
then the definition of $\NoLoc_s(r)$ gives
\[
M,p\Vdash \NoLoc_s(r).
\]

Assume instead that
\[
M,p\Vdash \LocSec_s(r).
\]
The formula $\CompSec_s(r)$ is also decided. If
\[
M,p\nVdash \CompSec_s(r),
\]
then
\[
M,p\Vdash \NoMatch_s(r)
\]
by definition. If
\[
M,p\Vdash \CompSec_s(r),
\]
then, together with
\[
M,p\nVdash \Sec_s(r),
\]
the definition of $\NoAmalg_s(r)$ gives
\[
M,p\Vdash \NoAmalg_s(r).
\]
Hence at least one failure case holds.

By \Cref{prop:null-modes-exclusive}, no two distinct cases can hold simultaneously. Therefore exactly one of the three cases holds.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Classification after refinement]\label{thm:null-classification-under-refinement}
Let
\[
q\le p,
\]
assume that the local-section predicates are decided at $q$ for the sort $s$, and let
\[
r:\mathsf{Ref}_s
\]
be admissible at $q$. If
\[
M,q\Vdash \NoGlob_s(r),
\]
then exactly one of the formulas
\[
\NoLoc_s(r),\qquad
\NoMatch_s(r),\qquad
\NoAmalg_s(r)
\]
holds at $q$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Apply \Cref{prop:null-trichotomy} at the refined state $q$.

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. +For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values.  \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal information-determining axis sets, so \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{proof}

For a component-gerbe class $\omega$, evaluation on $H_2$ gives $\operatorname{ev}_\omega:H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A$; its image and cokernel determine the componentwise and aggregate quotients.  When $H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0$ and $H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, the possible image subgroups are exactly those generated by at most $\beta$ elements.  Under explicit separatedness, representability, and \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison hypotheses, matching families without global amalgamations correspond to non-neutral component gerbes.  This derived $H^2$ invariant is not the relative \v{C}ech $H^1$ obstruction of Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa; only the underlying support-presheaf comparison is functorial, and the finite-group characterization does not transfer to bare empirical models.
 \end{abstract}

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal information-determining axis sets, so \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{proof}

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial.  \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal information-determining axis sets, so \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{proof}

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal information-determining axis sets, so \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{proof}

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal information-determining axis sets, so \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{proof}
