Thus every pullback demanded by the reference-refinement-site axioms is represented in the site, while the \v{C}ech cochains still ignore empty intersections because the constant sheaf has only the zero section on $\emptyset$. The pretopology is generated by these covers, their pullbacks, identity covers, and the empty cover of $\emptyset$, so any covering family in the generated site is refined by a common later barycentric open-star cover. This proves filteredness and cofinality.
 
 For \textup{(iii)}, the contractibility in \textup{(i)} makes each $\mathcal U^{(m)}$ a Leray cover for the genuine constant sheaf $G$ on the associated finite intersection site associated to the cover nerve. Empty pullback objects contribute no cochains. The Leray theorem for \v{C}ech cohomology therefore identifies the \v{C}ech cohomology of these covers with the sheaf cohomology of $|K|$, and the nerve identification in \textup{(i)} identifies the same groups with simplicial cohomology of $\operatorname{Sd}^mK$ \cite[Chap.~III, Sec.~4]{Bredon1997}, \cite[Sec.~4G]{Hatcher2002}. The refinement maps are the usual subdivision maps, hence induce cohomology isomorphisms.

\section{Concluding remarks}\label{sec:conclusion}

The paper separates three stages of the local-to-global problem. At the level
of information states, \Cref{thm:pointwise-irreducibility} shows that neither
existence of a matching family nor matching without amalgamation is definable
in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment considered
here. This is not a general expressivity theorem; it identifies the first
point at which the presheaf data exceed the lower language of universal team
satisfaction.

The passage from set-valued to groupoid-valued data necessarily depends on
additional lift data. By \Cref{thm:canonical-lift-rigidity}, a strictly
pullback-stable representative choice together with essential surjectivity on
the terminal fibre implies that the sheafification unit is surjective there.
Under $H^1$-vanishing and separatedness of the restriction to the slice site,
this is equivalent to the presheaf already satisfying the sheaf condition at
that fibre. For finite empirical models,
\Cref{thm:empirical-model-stack-interface} gives a canonical split banded
stack lift, but every component gerbe is neutral. The AMB obstruction is a
relative \v{C}ech $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section, whereas the
obstruction here is a derived Giraud $H^2$ class indexed by a global component
section. Only the support-level comparison is functorial, and neither class
recovers the other in general.

For a fixed finite nerve representative, the homological image
$K_\omega=\operatorname{Im}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)$ and homological
cokernel $Q_\omega=A/K_\omega$ record the contribution detected on $H_2$.
Across presentations they transport along chosen arrows in the
presentation-comparison groupoid; no independence of the chosen zigzag is
asserted. For several global component sections, the label-aware and
common-character quotients are related by the component-forgetting exact
sequence. Under the fixed finite-nerve, constant-band,
\v{C}ech-to-derived comparison, and $H_1=0$ hypotheses, the construction
theorems attain exactly the componentwise image subgroups permitted by
second homology.

When $H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, these are precisely
the subgroups generated by at most $\beta$ elements. The chosen open-star good
covers of a wedge of $\beta$ $2$-spheres therefore give the exact
classification: the nonzero finite abelian groups occurring as two-component
label-loss kernels with complementary nonzero image subgroups are those with
$d(G)\leq2\beta$ that are not cyclic $p$-groups. This construction does not
transfer to bare empirical models, whose canonical split lift has zero
homological image subgroups.

The hypotheses remain explicit throughout: \textup{(RC)} specifies pullbacks
of the presheaf data; \textup{(H1)}--\textup{(H4)} specify the banded lift,
representability, and \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison; separatedness is invoked
where global component sections are represented by matching families; and
$H^1$-vanishing is used for terminal-fibre rigidity. The formulation here uses
pullback-based slice sites. Comparisons of finite presentations are therefore
groupoid-indexed and zigzag-dependent, rather than presentation-free choices
of canonical representatives.

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal information-determining axis sets, so \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{proof}

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal information-determining axis sets, so \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{proof}

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal information-determining axis sets, so \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{proof}

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal information-determining axis sets, so \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{proof}

 \begin{document}
 
 \begin{abstract}
-A nonzero finite abelian group $G$ occurs as a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary nonzero image subgroups on the chosen good-cover site of a wedge of $\beta$ copies of $S^2$ if and only if $d(G)\leq 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.  This follows from the universal coefficient theorem after fixing a finite nerve, a constant finite abelian band, and a banded groupoid lift of a presheaf.  For a component-gerbe class $\omega$, evaluation on $H_2$ gives $\operatorname{ev}_\omega:H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A$; its image and cokernel determine the componentwise and aggregate quotients.  When $H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0$ and $H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, the possible image subgroups are exactly those generated by at most $\beta$ elements.  Under explicit separatedness, representability, and \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison hypotheses, matching families without global amalgamations correspond to non-neutral component gerbes.  This derived $H^2$ invariant is not the relative \v{C}ech $H^1$ obstruction of Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa; only the underlying support-presheaf comparison is functorial.

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial.  \end{proof}

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal information-determining axis sets, so \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{proof}

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal information-determining axis sets, so \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{proof}

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal information-determining axis sets, so \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{proof}

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal information-determining axis sets, so \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{proof}

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal information-determining axis sets, so \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{proof}

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal information-determining axis sets, so \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{proof}

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial.  \end{proof}

Under explicit separatedness, representability, and \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison hypotheses, matching families without global amalgamations correspond to non-neutral component gerbes.  This derived $H^2$ invariant is not the relative \v{C}ech $H^1$ obstruction of Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa; only the underlying support-presheaf comparison is functorial, and the finite-group characterization does not transfer to bare empirical models.
 \end{abstract}

 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]

-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. +For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause.  \end{proof}

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal information-determining axis sets, so \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{proof}

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial.  \end{proof}

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal information-determining axis sets, so \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{proof}

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial.  \end{proof}

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal information-determining axis sets, so \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{proof}

 \begin{abstract}

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal information-determining axis sets, so \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{proof}

 \begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
 Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item \textup{\textsc{Support}} belongs to coNP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} belongs to NP.
-\item \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
+\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
 \end{enumerate}
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For \textup{\textsc{Support}}, non-support is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and force opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Support}} is in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to force opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{Indispensable}} lies in NP.
+For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.
 
-For \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}}, the condition that $K$ supports $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is indispensable is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal support, so \textup{\textsc{MinSupport}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
+For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial.  \end{proof}
